newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Oct 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Oct 16.

text.p: Prepared by The Broadcast Monitoring Company for Reuters
-- UK CAR INDUSTRY GETS 750M STG BOOST

Three carmakers chose the Motor Show in Birmingham on Tuesday to announce new projects involving over 750m stg of investment in Britain. Land Rover is to produce a smaller version of its Discovery 4-wheel drive vehicle, securing 10,000 motor industry jobs over the next 10 years. Vauxhall is to invest 300m stg by 1998 on restructuring and expanding its plant at Ellesmere Port, Merseyside. And Blackpool-based specialist sports car maker TVR has launched two new engines and expects output of its three model range to rise by 50 per cent this year.
-- UNITED'S 593M STG BID WINS THE BATTLE FOR BLENHEIM

Exhibitions organise Blenheim has recommended a 592.5m stg bid from United News & Media to take a controlling stake in the group. The move follows months of speculation over possible bids, and heads off a possible bidding war with Dutch publishing and information group VNU which last week took a 14.99 per cent stake in Blenheim. United already has a trades magazines and exhibitions division, and the move will create the world's largest exhibitions organiser.
-- INNTREPRENEUR FACES LAW SUITS FROM TENANTS

The Inntrepreneur chain of public houses is facing an increasing number of law suits from tenants over allegedly high rents and beer prices. Up to 400 tenants are understood to have initiated or be considering legal actions. The company, however, which owns and leases 2,900 pubs, says it is only aware of 114 cases which have been filed.
-- GREENBURY EXECUTIVE PAY POLICY IGNORED, PANEL SAYS

A report from the independent corporate governance consultancy PIRC claims that British companies have paid out more than 68m stg in compensation to directors who have resigned or accepted less favorable terms in the past three years. The survey reveals that many companies have ignored the recommendations of the Greenbury committee on executive pay by making the large compensation payments. Sir Richard Greenbury, chairman of the committee on executive pay, has criticised the PIRC report as selective and premature.
-- WATER SHARES DIP OVER 'EXPECTED' PRICE REVIEW

An announcement on Tuesday by water industry regulator Ian Byatt that he will conduct a mid-term review of prices in the industry in 1999 prompted a fall in shares in water and sewage companies. However, the interim price review had been widely expected, and at least one water company spokesman, David Luffrum of Thames Water, expressed surprise at the market reaction to the announcement.
-- GAS CONTRACTS VERDICT OVERTURNED

The Court of Appeal has overturned a lower court judgement involving a dispute between National Power and United Gas, clearing the way for a similar dispute over 'take-or-pay' gas contracts in the North Sea to move to full trial. The United Gas case has been closely tracked by the gas industry as it covers issues similar to those in the bitter contest between British Gas and North Sea gas producers over some 40bn stg worth of contracts.
-- NYNEX AND TELEWEST END TALKS ON MERGER

Merger talks between Britain's largest and second-largest cable groups - Telewest and Nynex CableComms respectively - have been broken off after more than a year of discussions. It is understood that the two companies had been close to agreement on a merger, a move which would have created a company better able to compete against satellite rival BSkyB. -- INCHCAPE SELLS BAIN HOGG TO AON FOR 160M STG

International trading group Inchcape has agreed to sell its Bain Hogg insurance broking subsidiary to Aon Corporation of the US for 160m stg. Inchcape had been expected to demerge Bain Hogg, and the sale was completed just hours before it was due to have published particulars of the demerger plan. Last week Inchape also disposed of Testing Services for 380m stg, and the combined revenue from both sales will wipe out the group's borrowings.
-- NEWS CORP TO FLOAT TV TECHNOLOGY DIVISION

Media giant News Corporation has announced plans to float its UK-based television technology business News Digital Systems (NDS) within the next two to three weeks. NDS is a leading manufacturer of 'smart-card' decoders needed to access pay-TV broadcasts, and also owns technology for compressing TV signals to allow a number of digital channels to be carried in space which previously carried just one.
-- SUPERSCAPE SIGNS LICENSING DEAL

Superscape VR has signed a licensing and distribution deal with Microsoft for its Viscape 3-D web browser. Viscape will now be including in the Internet Explorer Kit distributed with Windows 95, and users will be given allowed a 60-day free trial before deciding whether to pay $29 over the Internet. Superscape, which reported annual pre-tax losses of 2.87m stg on Tuesday, also has agreements and partnerships with IBM and Silicon Graphics.
